subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed nonzero exec exits be normal agent-observable results by default, or should only explicit accepted exit codes suppress tool-error classification?
rationale: Current main already treats normal nonzero process exits as completed at the exec runtime layer, but the shared classifier and cron path still treat them as errors; changing that default has compatibility impact for workflows that currently depend on nonzero exits being failures.

options.title: Default completed-exit semantics
options.body: Treat ordinary reason=exit subprocess exits as non-tool-failure results by default, preserving stdout/stderr plus exitCode for the agent while keeping spawn, timeout, signal, and shell 126/127 failures on the error path.

options.title: Opt-in accepted exit codes
options.body: Add an explicit accepted-exit-code policy for workflows that need semantic nonzero exits while preserving current failure behavior by default.

options.title: Document the wrapper workaround
options.body: Keep current behavior and document the always-exit-zero wrapper pattern, accepting the ongoing cron prompt burden and user confusion.

recommendation.title: Default completed-exit semantics
recommendation.body: Treat ordinary reason=exit subprocess exits as non-tool-failure results by default, preserving stdout/stderr plus exitCode for the agent while keeping spawn, timeout, signal, and shell 126/127 failures on the error path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history points to steipete as the strongest recent carrier for the shared classifier/runtime files and this choice is a cross-surface product contract decision.
